metadata.scope: 15 provisional flagship source reviews and 1 calendar diversity substitution
metadata.method: Cross-check core event/date/location, preserve original NCEI segment IDs, record source dependency, never approve numeric claims or image rights automatically.

reviews.title_after: Beauregard–Smiths Station EF4 tornado strikes Alabama
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NCEI Bupree is a Lee County segment of the Beauregard–Smiths Station tornado. NWS verifies March 3 and EF4 identity.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: Do not sum Bupree county-level casualties with the entire tornado. Rating and 170 mph are survey-based estimates, not measured 10 m gusts.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Trace Macon–Lee counties using the NWS surveyed path, marking EF4 damage locations rather than treating the entire track as EF4.

reviews.title_after: Rolling Fork–Silver City EF4 tornado crosses the Mississippi Delta
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NCEI Egremont segment is part of the March 24 Rolling Fork–Silver City tornado; MEMA independently documents community impacts and date.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: The NCEI event begins near Egremont; this is not an independent second storm. Separate first reports, final 195 mph rating and final casualty scope.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Show the single long-track tornado through Egremont, Rolling Fork and Silver City using an original surveyed-track map.

reviews.title_before: Tornado — Ragland to 5 NE Rock, Alabama
reviews.title_after: The 1994 Palm Sunday tornado destroys Goshen United Methodist Church
reviews.corroborating_publisher: CDC Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: The 1994 F4 tornado began near Ragland and reached the Goshen church north of Piedmont during Palm Sunday worship; CDC independently documents casualties.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: Published contemporary casualty counts were updated; CDC 20 church fatalities refers to the church, not automatically the whole tornado or outbreak. Distinct from 1965 Palm Sunday outbreak on Apr 11.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Construct a Ragland–Piedmont geographic path and a careful warning/impact timeline; confirm 1994 EST/CST usage.

reviews.title_after: The April 8, 1998 Oak Grove F5 tornado hits central Alabama
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NWS documents an F5 tornado affecting Oak Grove and western Jefferson County on April 8, 1998; NCEI's Oak Grove record is a location segment.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: An F5 is the pre-2007 Fujita rating, NOT EF5. Multiple tornadoes occurred that day; distinguish this path from other members of the outbreak.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Build a surveyed track and damage gradient against historical Jefferson County communities; historical photos not cleared.

reviews.title_after: The Tuscaloosa–Birmingham EF4 tornado devastates Alabama
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NCEI Ralph, Alabama describes the long-track EF4 across Greene, Tuscaloosa and Jefferson Counties on April 27, 2011.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: Do not conflate one EF4 with the entire 2011 Super Outbreak. Published fatalities and wind estimates may use county segment versus total track denominators.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Plot the Tuscaloosa–Birmingham path on an original map; distinguish EF4 maximum rating from EF4 damage along every mile.

reviews.title_after: Picher–Neosho EF4 tornado crosses Oklahoma into Missouri
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NCEI Hornet, Missouri is a downstream segment of the May 10, 2008 Picher–Neosho EF4 tornado; NWS Springfield follows the cross-state track.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: May 10 is a local date on both sides of state line; do not sum Missouri fatalities with Picher Oklahoma counts without separate scopes. EF4 survey estimates not measured winds.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Create cross-border track map with measured NWS tornado path; annotate county segment boundaries.

reviews.title_after: The Newcastle–Moore EF5 tornado devastates central Oklahoma
reviews.corroborating_publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NIST conducted independent post-storm building and life-safety reconnaissance of the May 20, 2013 Newcastle–Moore EF5 tornado.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: NIST documents facilities and communications, not an independently measured EF5 wind speed. NCEI Moore is a county segment crossing from McClain to Cleveland.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Combine NWS path outline with clearly sourced school/critical-facility performance notes, without unlicensed photography.

reviews.title_after: The Joplin EF5 tornado strikes southwestern Missouri
reviews.corroborating_publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NCEI Central City record documents a segment of the May 22, 2011 Joplin EF5, while NIST conducted independent engineering, warning and human-response investigations.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: Different fatality counts reflect differing cutoffs and inclusion of subsequent deaths. Do not treat a Central City segment narrative as citywide impact statistics.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Plot the surveyed Joplin track with separate, attributed NIST warning and structural-vulnerability annotations.

reviews.title_after: Fifteen tornadoes strike Indiana during a late-November outbreak
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: Indiana's November 22, 1992 late-season tornado outbreak is separately cataloged in national historical tornado reports, consistent with NWS Indianapolis's dated case study.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: The secondary site compiles SPC/NWS records and is not independent track measurement. Do not assume 15 Indiana tornadoes equals outbreak-wide count across states.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Plot a newly sourced state tornado track map, keeping NWS Indiana total distinct from national storm-day totals.

reviews.title_before: 1950 Great Appalachian Storm and the Snow Bowl
reviews.title_after: The Great Appalachian Storm meets the Ohio State–Michigan Snow Bowl
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: Ohio State's archive independently places the Snow Bowl football game amid the November 25, 1950 Great Appalachian Storm documented by NWS.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: A football-game account corroborates on-campus snow and its date, not all regional snow totals. Storm evolved over Nov 24–29, with different local snowfall windows.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Contrast original weather maps and verified station snowfall with clearly attributed archival OSU game photographs (rights still pending).

reviews.title_after: Unusual December tornadoes hit east-central Wisconsin in 1970
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: County emergency management independently lists a December 1, 1970 Medina-area F3 tornado, supporting the broader NWS Green Bay outbreak date.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: Outagamie County uses the modern 'EF-3' notation for an event rated in the original Fujita scale; public copy should say F3 (retrospective source terminology) after record check. County count not the statewide count.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Original map of historic county tornado paths emphasizing rare December timing and historical Fujita classification.

reviews.title_after: The 1978 Bossier City F4 tornado strikes before dawn
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: Tornado Talk reviews the December 3, 1978 Bossier City F4 and refers to Fujita's original study; NWS Shreveport documents timing and path.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: Independent author site uses original Fujita/NWS material; don't treat rating as new measurement. Distinguish Shreveport/Bossier track from other tornadoes that morning.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Recreate the 1978 path along the Red River with contemporary city streets using georeferenced original track references.

reviews.title_after: The December 2021 western Kentucky EF4 tornado crosses Mayfield
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: The NCEI Baltimore, Kentucky segment belongs to the long-track western Kentucky EF4 of December 10–11, 2021, including Mayfield.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: Separate local December 10 evening from December 11 early hours and distinguish continuous EF4 track from separate tornadoes spawned by the supercell; track-specific casualty totals unverified.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Create original county-by-county track timeline across Dec 10–11 using exact local/UTC annotations.

reviews.title_after: The December 16, 2000 Tuscaloosa F4 tornado crosses Alabama
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NCEI Hull, Alabama is a location segment of the December 16, 2000 Tuscaloosa F4 tornado, independently retold in dated Alabama weather coverage.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: Use F4 (pre-2007 scale), not EF4. Fatality and path totals must be scoped to the whole tornado and verified rather than copied from this one county record.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Plot full southwest Tuscaloosa County path with survey legend and distinguish maximum F4 from every point's damage.

reviews.title_after: A violent EF4 tornado tears through Garland and Rowlett, Texas
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: An industry engineering team conducted independent building-damage assessments following the December 26, 2015 Sunnyvale–Garland–Rowlett EF4; NCEI New Hope is a reporting segment.
reviews.unverified_claims_and_cautions: Do not equate observed EF4 damage at Garland with EF4 damage along all 13 miles. APA's building observations are not an independent radar wind field; fatality totals differ by entire outbreak versus this tornado.
reviews.original_visual_concept: Construct original damage-path outline with distinct residential structural-failure mechanisms from APA survey.

primary_replacements.reason: Avoid same-hazard triple feature May 27–29 with separately sourced historic river flooding.
primary_replacements.graphic_type: Original dated river-stage hydrograph and satellite comparison
primary_replacements.limitations: May28 reached above previous flood record, but was NOT the final flood crest (later May30-31). NASA images dated May 27 and May 28 explicitly; do not mislabel those satellite dates or reuse without per-asset rights. NASA stage figure derives from hydrometric source, not a second independent gauge. Replaces 2019 Linwood EF4 tornado as primary to avoid May27-29 triple-tornado sequence; previous primary preserved: phasea-pass2-2019-05-28.

followup_quality_items: Two previously held lead IDs per date remain unverified, and independent alternate corroboration is still zero.
Source-dependency review: 15 second URL additions are not 15 independent atmospheric measurements.
Tornado-rich flagship category needs deliberate yearly hazard rotation and occurrence-versus-impact date integrity.
Research 258 remaining single-source primaries, prioritizing interesting geographic and historical diversity rather than simply adding URLs.
